records.CRITICISM: Lean universalism and the caricature of mass production
records.EVIDENCE: Early critics disputed IMVP's economic reasoning, plant comparisons and universal-best-way claims; later genealogy and contingency work narrowed the claim.
records.VALID_CORE: Cross-plant configurations can outperform alternatives under some conditions.
records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Reject universal superiority; retain mechanism-by-mechanism, context-bound evaluation.

records.CRITICISM: 'Lean and mean' cost cutting, layoffs and trust destruction
records.EVIDENCE: Toyota's own history records 1950 job-cut conflict; labour research links some Lean deployments to reduced autonomy, intensification and poorer well-being.
records.VALID_CORE: Productivity and avoidable-cost reduction can be legitimate.
records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Evaluate credible employment/redeployment commitments, workload and distribution of gains where improvement asks workers to expose labor-saving opportunities. These are contextual and normative safeguards, not a demonstrated universally necessary causal package; harmful deployments remain admissible evidence.

records.CRITICISM: Coercive standardisation and deskilling
records.EVIDENCE: Standardised work can support visibility and training, but longitudinal evidence links formalisation/assembly Lean to reduced autonomy and skill use.
records.VALID_CORE: An explicit current baseline enables comparison and learning.
records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Retain a useful baseline with proportionate exception and revision rights; treat explicit expiry/retirement as analytical safeguards when needed. records.CRITICISM: Low inventory and JIT brittleness
records.EVIDENCE: Operations science requires buffering variability; inventory-performance can be concave; disruption cases expose tier opacity and long recovery.

records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Distinguish inventory/capacity/time buffering from information and alternate-capability enablers. Choose a feasible portfolio by criticality, lead time and turbulence; neither JIT nor stockpiling alone guarantees resilience.

records.CRITICISM: A3, Five Whys or PDCA templates substitute for causal inquiry
records.EVIDENCE: Inspected methodological criticism challenges linear causal narratives and weak controls. PDSA reporting often omitted core features; S047 did not test whether method fidelity caused better outcomes, and poor reporting alone does not establish absent practice.
records.VALID_CORE: Compact reasoning and iterative testing can be valuable.
records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Retain evidence-bound causal models, explicit predictions and qualified countermeasures; no named template has intrinsic evidentiary force.

records.CRITICISM: Stop-the-line creates false stops, alarm fatigue or production avoidance

records.CRITICISM: Respect-for-people doctrine diverges from observed practice

records.EVOLVED_DISPOSITION: Treat respect claims as testable work-design conditions, not an authenticity shield or presumed benefit.
